races.name: Racing Again 14th September Maiden Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Rock Armour
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse with David Thompson's yard in a 1/9 recent form for the trainer — form figures are uninspiring (5,5,6,5,3) over longer trips, and while going poses no concern, the staying trip and naturally rear-positioned style mean he needs something to go wrong up front to get involved.|

runners_data.name: Way Maker
runners_data.note: Mickey Bowen's front-runner carries a hood (headgear flagged) and has strong similar-going credentials (2W5P from 8 runs), making this small-field, uncontested lead scenario ideal — a 25-day absence is not a concern given consistent recent form and the trainer running at 6/18 in the last 14 days.|

runners_data.name: Earnest Belief
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's charge has five consecutive third-place finishes and genuine consistency, but as a true hold-up type pushed forward to midfield on the map, it will not naturally secure a prominent pitch — its chance depends on a strong pace developing, which looks unlikely in this small field, tempering optimism despite its tidy form.|

runners_data.name: Datstheholyallofit
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes takes the ride on this Patrick Neville-trained five-year-old who won on similar going (1W3P from 5 comparable runs) and whose recent form (44-123, including a win) shows clear improvement — prominent style suits this scenario ideally, and 12 days since last run is no obstacle.|

runners_data.name: Ocean Rose
runners_data.note: Barry John Murphy's mare has finished sixth in all three career starts with zero wins or placings on similar going, making it hard to construct a positive scenario — a 58-day layoff and Callum Pritchard aboard represent insufficient compensating factors for her deeply unencouraging form profile.|

races.paceDynamic: Way Maker is the sole confirmed front-runner and will set off to lead from the outset over this 2m5f trip at Sedgefield on Good ground, dictating a sustainable gallop without any meaningful pressure from rivals. Datstheholyallofit is the only horse likely to push forward and challenge for early position, tracking Way Maker prominently, but with just five runners the race is unlikely to develop a truly contested pace. Rock Armour and Ocean Rose are natural hold-up types who will be anchored at the rear, while Earnest Belief, a genuine hold-up horse redistributed to midfield on the map, is unlikely to secure a truly prominent position and will race closer to the hold-up group than its map slot suggests. This shape — a lone front-runner controlling a modest gallop in a small field over a staying trip — strongly favours horses who can track the pace in a handy position and sustain their effort through the final stages, giving the prominent-to-midfield profile the clearest tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Way Maker Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Way Maker leads unchallenged and sets a steady, controlled gallop that rewards horses travelling prominently.
scenarios.body: Way Maker dictates from the front at a manageable pace over 2m5f on Good ground, allowing Datstheholyallofit to track in a perfect stalking position and pounce approaching the final hurdle. This scenario is the dominant race shape: a lone front-runner in a five-runner field over a staying trip on a fair surface is precisely the setup that rewards the horse sitting second or third and travelling within itself.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Way Maker's controlled lead proves too comfortable and rivals fail to close the gap.
scenarios.body: Way Maker, settled and uncontested through the early and middle stages, builds an insurmountable advantage as hold-up rivals are asked to find form too late in the contest. The modest field and lack of pace pressure means Way Maker's natural front-running instincts are fully exploited, and with good recent similar-going form (2W5P), a wire-to-wire success is credible.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently in the final half-mile to bring the hold-up horses into play.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected gallop from Way Maker, possibly under pressure from Datstheholyallofit, could string the field out and create enough of a test for Rock Armour or Earnest Belief to close from behind. However, Earnest Belief is not truly positioned at the rear and Rock Armour's form figures (5,12,6,5,3) suggest limited ability to capitalise, so this scenario carries low probability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Collapses, Outsider Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses underperform or fall and the contest is reduced to a scramble.
scenarios.body: Ocean Rose, with a form string of three consecutive sixth-place finishes and no wins or placings on similar going, would only feature if the race fell apart entirely around her. This is a low-probability scenario that relies on chaos rather than form, but in a five-runner field any incident significantly reshapes outcomes.

watchPoints.text: Way Maker's uncontested lead is the race-defining factor — if Datstheholyallofit pushes forward aggressively early, even a minor increase in pace could unsettle Way Maker's rhythm and open the race up.

Earnest Belief's natural hold-up tendency means Brian Hughes on Datstheholyallofit and James Bowen on Way Maker are likely to get soft early positions — watch whether Earnest Belief drifts back further than its mapped position suggests and loses touch.

Rock Armour has not won in similar going across 6 runs (0W2P) and is operating at a distance slightly beyond its best historical form — watch for whether it travels with any fluency in the final mile.
Ocean Rose's 58-day absence, combined with a form string of three consecutive sixths and zero placed efforts on Good, means any positive market move should be treated with significant caution.
Way Maker's hood (headgear flagged) is worth monitoring in the paddock — if the horse appears unsettled or keen pre-race, its ability to conserve energy in front over 2m5f could be compromised.

races.name: Roxyfet Sports Lounge For Private Hire Mares' Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Spot On Soph
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old hold-up mare trained by Sam England who has shown consistent form at this sort of trip on good ground (2nd and 3rd in recent good-ground runs), though 173 days off the track is a significant fitness concern and amateur rider Miss Hitchen (10lb claim) adds uncertainty at this level.
runners_data.comment: Ranked top of nine on our rating, Spot On Soph has run over today's trip and going and her second and third in recent starts mark her out as a genuine threat at 168 lb, though she arrives winless and 173 days between runs is the main concern.

runners_data.name: O'Faolains Glory
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner who sets the pace shape for everyone else, though her trainer has just 0 wins from 1 runner in the last 14 days and her last six runs show a sharp drop in form — the tag noting she is racing out of role (STYLE_FIT 0.93) is a mild flag but the lead is hers to lose regardless.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins two and three starts back give O'Faolains Glory a solid recent profile, and she returns after 25 days in good order with distance and going experience in her favour; two unimpressive efforts since temper expectations slightly under 168 lb.

runners_data.name: Asa
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's seven-year-old hold-up type who was unexpectedly beaten a long way last time on good ground at Uttoxeter, but her win at 25f on soft and place at 26f on good suggests this 20f trip on good may be just short of her best distance; 7lb claimer Miss Cookson adds some intrigue.
runners_data.comment: Asa landed a win three starts back and was third two starts back, showing she retains the ability to mix it at this level, and she has experience of today's distance and going; the main concern is a 149-day absence carrying 167 lb.

runners_data.name: Stellarmasterpiece
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes the ride on this rapidly improving six-year-old who has won four of her last five starts, all on good ground and all in the prominent position that suits her perfectly — the headgear flag (p) confirms she has raced in a hood and the form string 55-111 reads like a horse coming sharply to hand.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of nine on our figures, Stellarmasterpiece faces a stiff ask under 161 lb, yet her recent form is hard to ignore — three wins in her last five starts, including victories in her last three, and she has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Lone Star
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old Philip Kirby mare who races prominently and has 13 of 15 good-ground runs to her name, giving her strong course-conditions fitness, though her recent form figures of 0-5437 show she has not found the winner's enclosure since a single win at 18f and the last-time 7th at Uttoxeter was modest.
runners_data.comment: Lone Star arrives on the back of a third two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, with her rating of 101 putting her right in the mix as a leading danger; the concern is a winless recent run of five starts and a hefty 159 lb to shoulder.

runners_data.name: Curious Mrs Fox
runners_data.note: David Thompson's five-year-old hold-up filly has placed twice from five good-ground starts and is lightly handicapped on OR 84, with the 5lb claim from Thompson junior potentially relevant; all her runs have been at 16-20f and she may appreciate the step back up from shorter trips.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Curious Mrs Fox showed promise with a runner-up finish last time out after 45 days off, and she has run over today's trip and going before, though she shoulders 152 lb here.

runners_data.name: Yanka Blue
runners_data.note: Barry John Murphy's five-year-old has strong recent place form (2nd twice in her last four) and her true running style is hold-up, though the field's depth of hold-up horses means she is effectively pushed into a midfield position she would not naturally choose — the 0.90 style-fit flag tempers confidence, and a 12-day turnaround at least suggests freshness is not an issue.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Yanka Blue makes it hard to build a case; she has run over today's trip and going before, and the return to form that produced two seconds in her recent starts shows ability, but the latest seventh is a concern.

runners_data.name: Dusky Spyglass
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who wears headgear (h) and whose natural instinct is to race from behind, but returning from 182 days off is a major question mark over fitness at this trip on good ground; with incomplete form figures in her history she is difficult to assess and the redistribution into midfield further complicates her tactical picture.
runners_data.comment: Dusky Spyglass has run over today's going before, yet two pulled-up efforts in her last four starts raise fitness and jumping questions after 182 days absent, and carrying 145 lb won't help a mare who remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Brooklyn Lullaby
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby's six-year-old has recorded a 2nd at 18f on good and a 5th at 20f recently, suggesting the distance is fine, but her genuine hold-up style is squeezed by the crowded rear of this field — trainer has 4 wins from 33 runners in 14 days suggesting decent yard form, and a 21-day turnaround is straightforward.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Brooklyn Lullaby faces a stiff ask here, though second two starts back shows she can get competitive and she arrives fit on 21 days' rest with distance and going experience in her favour.

races.paceDynamic: O'Faolains Glory is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will dictate a controlled, honest gallop from the front over Sedgefield's 2m4f trip on good ground. Stellarmasterpiece and Lone Star are the natural prominent types who will sit closest to her, creating a small lead group with the remainder of the field — Spot On Soph, Asa, Curious Mrs Fox, Yanka Blue, Dusky Spyglass, and Brooklyn Lullaby — strung out behind. This is an uncontested pace scenario: O'Faolains Glory sets a sustainable tempo that is unlikely to be pressured or quickened into, which classically rewards horses who can travel prominently or make smooth headway from midfield rather than true hold-up closers who need a strong end-to-end gallop to pick off tired rivals. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Yanka Blue, Dusky Spyglass, and Brooklyn Lullaby are all genuine hold-up horses who will be forced to race closer than ideal, with Yanka Blue and Brooklyn Lullaby the most likely to actually secure a midfield berth while Dusky Spyglass, having been off 182 days, may find herself further back than connections want. The race shape decisively favours prominent and close-tracking profiles who can keep tabs on a lone front-runner and pounce at the second-last without needing a cavalry charge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prompt Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If O'Faolains Glory dictates an uncontested, moderate pace and prominent racers make their move from the second-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: O'Faolains Glory bowls along in front with Stellarmasterpiece and Lone Star breathing down her neck, and one of the prominent trackers produces a clean jump at the last to assert; the steady tempo means no one is running on empty and it becomes a battle of acceleration from the front of the field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If O'Faolains Glory's uncontested lead proves impossible to reel in and she simply wins on the bridle from the front.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing or able to press her, O'Faolains Glory conserves energy throughout and simply quickens away from the last hurdle before anyone can close the gap; her recent win form on soft suggests she handles good well enough and an uncontested lead flatters any front-runner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough mid-race to leave front-runners vulnerable, allowing a hold-up horse to sweep through.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the prominent trio to push the tempo between them and tie each other up, creating a genuine target for a closer; Spot On Soph or Asa, both legitimate hold-up types with good-ground form, are best placed to exploit this, but the uncontested pace dynamic makes it an unlikely outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Stellarmasterpiece and Lone Star both push O'Faolains Glory hard early, creating a tactical battle between the lead group.
scenarios.body: A contested pace between three prominent types would suit a fresh closer tracking just behind, but the redistribution of Yanka Blue and Brooklyn Lullaby into midfield means the genuine closers are compromised in their position; the scenario is possible but depends on jockey decisions that current evidence does not strongly support.

watchPoints.text: Stellarmasterpiece is the standout danger — four wins from her last five on good ground, prominent style perfectly suited to tracking O'Faolains Glory, and Sean Bowen in the saddle; watch whether she is close enough at the second-last to mount an unanswered challenge.

O'Faolains Glory's recent form figures of 9-10-4-1-1 show sharp regression after her winning sequence, and if she sets only a modest gallop from the front she could be vulnerable to Stellarmasterpiece and Lone Star sweeping past her before the last.

Yanka Blue, Dusky Spyglass, and Brooklyn Lullaby are all natural hold-up horses forced into a midfield berth by the race shape — watch for traffic issues on Sedgefield's turning track if they get bunched together on the bend before the home straight.

Dusky Spyglass returns from 182 days off the track; watch for signs of rustiness at the early hurdles, as an error under the headgear from cold could settle the result of any tight finish before the straight is even reached.

The 10lb and 5lb amateur/conditional claims of Miss Hitchen and Joshua Thompson are meaningful in a field of this level — watch whether the weight advantage translates into a market move and whether either can hold a clean position through Sedgefield's tight bends.

races.name: Christmas Parties At Sedgefield Racecourse Handicap Steeple Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Glenmalure Flyer
runners_data.note: Recent winner over 28f on Good (Harry Skelton up), sits in behind the pace as a prominent racer — the Skelton combination are in strong form (T14: 9/23) and this horse's sim-going record (8/13, 2W3P) and trip profile make him a live player if the front pair set it up.
runners_data.comment: Glenmalure Flyer won last time out and has won three times in her last five starts, with her trainer firing at 39% in the past fortnight and she has run on today's going before; the main risk is carrying 163 lb.

runners_data.name: Thank You Blue
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has been placed nine times from fifteen runs on similar going without winning (0W3P), suggesting a tendency to do plenty of work without always finishing it off — the presence of Limerick Leader directly challenging for the lead is a significant threat to his stamina reserves late on.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and lightly tried at the top of the weights, Thank You Blue has finished second twice and third three starts back in recent starts, and he returns on going he has already encountered just 12 days on — winless in his last five but the one to beat on our rating.

runners_data.name: Limerick Leader
runners_data.note: Returned just five days ago but has the best recent form in the race (-23341) and an outstanding similar-going record (12/15, 2W10P); wears tongue strap alongside blinkers, and as the lower-rated leader (OR=96) is weighted to run a big race — the key question is whether a 5-day turnaround leaves him fully fresh at this stamina-testing trip.
runners_data.comment: Limerick Leader advertises solid recent form — a winner last time out and placed efforts threading through his last five starts — and he has run over today's trip and going before, so conditions hold no fears; the concern is whether five days is enough recovery time carrying 158 lb.

runners_data.name: Sir Carnegie
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up horse (Sean Bowen, T14: 6/18) racing just two days after his last run, which is an unusually quick turnaround and merits scrutiny; three wins at 24f on Good are encouraging for this trip, but his style demands maximum pace carnage ahead of him — if the front-runners don't truly exhaust each other, his late run may fall just short.
runners_data.comment: Sir Carnegie won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims here, and a rating of 106 underlines his threat; the main concern is whether two days since that victory leaves him short of full recovery.

races.paceDynamic: Thank You Blue and Limerick Leader are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 3m2½f trip at Sedgefield, creating a genuinely competitive pace rather than a solo march. With both horses wanting to dictate on Good ground — a surface both handle comfortably — the early exchanges will be honest at minimum and potentially pressured, eating into reserves before the final fences. Sir Carnegie, the hold-up horse in the field, will be tracking from off the pace with Sean Bowen plotting a patient route, while Glenmalure Flyer will look to sit prominently just behind the two leaders and pounce. This race shape — two front-runners burning each other up over a stamina-testing trip — most favours hold-up and prominent-off-the-pace profiles who can conserve energy and pounce late, with Sir Carnegie's style ideally suited and Glenmalure Flyer well-positioned to capitalise if the leaders tie each other up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Suits Stalkers
scenarios.trigger: If Thank You Blue and Limerick Leader push each other along at a strong clip, setting up a true stamina test in the final half mile.
scenarios.body: The two leaders burn each other off over this extended trip on Good ground, leaving them vulnerable inside the final two fences as their reserves are depleted. Prominent and hold-up horses who have been tracking at a comfortable rhythm arrive with energy to spare and outstay the tiring front pair.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If Limerick Leader or Thank You Blue establishes a clear advantage early and the other capitulates, allowing a controlled solo gallop.
scenarios.body: A settled, uncontested gallop over this trip would dramatically change the calculus — the leader retains enough in reserve to kick on safely approaching the last two fences. Limerick Leader, who has the better recent form string (-23341) and strongest similar-going record (12/15), is the likelier candidate to assume control if Thank You Blue weakens.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Glenmalure Flyer travels powerfully in behind the pace duel and produces a clean jumping round to assert from two out.
scenarios.body: Harry Skelton keeps Glenmalure Flyer close enough to the pace that the horse never has to make a decisive move too early, then delivers a well-timed run on the back of the leaders' attrition. On this trip and going, with a recent win at 28f on Good in the book, the distance and surface are no concern.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly ferocious and Sir Carnegie is produced with one sweeping late run to catch rivals on the line.
scenarios.body: Sean Bowen would need to time a near-perfect late challenge from last place, relying on the leaders having gone hard enough to fall apart in the final stages. Sir Carnegie's OR=101 and course form are solid but a 2-day turnaround and the reliance on maximum pace attrition introduce meaningful uncertainty.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Thank You Blue or Limerick Leader flinches first at the head of affairs — if one caves before halfway, the other may steal an uncontested lead and completely transform the race shape.

Sir Carnegie's 2-day turnaround is strikingly short and connections should be monitored; if he shows any sign of stiffness or sluggishness at the start, his hold-up role becomes even harder to execute over 3m2½f.

Limerick Leader's 5-day return is also quick — watch his demeanour in the paddock and at the start; he wore blinkers and a tongue strap last time and those headgear pointers suggest he needs to be switched on mentally.

Glenmalure Flyer has the best combination of pace proximity and stamina at this trip — watch whether Harry Skelton allows him to creep closer than usual to the front two between the 2m and 3m marks, as that would signal an earlier-than-expected challenge.

With only four runners and Good ground, the race is unlikely to be run at a crawl — but if there is an unexpected early tardy pace, Glenmalure Flyer's prominent style means he is best placed to exploit it, which would flip the outcome away from the hold-up profile.

races.name: Winning Connections Conference Hire Handicap Steeple Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Westerton
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning on 18-day turnaround for Jennie Candlish, who has only one winner from 15 runners in the past fortnight; handles good ground (1 place from 1 run on similar going) but the combination of an off-pace style and a congested rear makes getting a clean run difficult here.
runners_data.comment: Westerton ran a solid second three starts back and returns on a quick turnaround of 18 days with experience of today's trip and going, making him a genuine danger at 168 lb; the pulled-up run two starts back is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Hooper
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old with six places from his past 15 runs on good ground and handled good going well in his last start, but the amateur claimer (7lb) is a significant factor at this level; natural hold-up style means he must overcome a crowded midfield, though his proven placed consistency makes him one to respect if he gets a clear passage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but has shown ability, finishing second three starts back, and that run — combined with experience over today's trip and going — makes Hooper the one to assess highly here; a rating of 111 puts him clear at the top of this nine-runner field.

runners_data.name: Socks Off
runners_data.note: Returning after a 232-day absence for Kevin & Lauren Frost, which is a significant fitness flag in a jumps handicap; her recent form string of three placings on good ground shows she stays and handles the conditions, but a hold-up runner coming back from such a layoff will need things to go perfectly — treat with caution until she proves her fitness.
runners_data.comment: Socks Off has shown admirable consistency, placing third three times in recent starts, and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating of 103 suggesting he holds strong claims here; the main concern is a 232-day absence under 166 lb.

runners_data.name: Dexter
runners_data.note: Strong trainer form with Oliver Greenall & Josh Guerriero sending out 2 from 12 in 14 days; his best form comes on good ground (14 from 15 runs) and he carries a tongue tie and cheek pieces, but he is a genuine rear-of-field operator who will be squeezed into midfield by the volume of hold-up types, blunting his typical late-finishing threat.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Dexter nonetheless showed encouragement with a third last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, though 164 lb is a stern ask for a gelding yet to find the winner's enclosure.

runners_data.name: American Empire
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a win and five places on good going from 12 similar-going runs, trained by Donald McCain who is out of form at 0 from 13 in the past fortnight; holds up naturally but must race in an unnatural midfield position given the congestion, and that compromised role reduces confidence in his finishing effort despite the consistent form figures.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, American Empire at least brings consistent placing to the table — third on three occasions in recent starts — though back-to-back sevenths and fifths suggest he may be finding it tough to recapture that form; experience over today's trip and going offers some encouragement at 163 lb.

runners_data.name: Getaway Jewel
runners_data.note: The sole pace-setter in the race: Micky Hammond sends her back just nine days after her last run (trainer 2 from 10 in 14 days), and her record of 2 wins and 9 places on good ground from 15 runs underlines she is well-suited to today's conditions; with no pressing rival, Hughes can control every yard of this from the front.
runners_data.comment: Rated well below the field on our figures and ranked last of nine, Getaway Jewel is hard to fancy despite a win two starts back and experience over today's trip and going; only a 9-day turnaround and an active recent profile count mildly in his favour.

runners_data.name: Applejack Poet
runners_data.note: Barry John Murphy runner with 0 wins but 3 places from 15 good-ground runs, and the recent form includes a pulled-up effort which warrants scrutiny; he races prominently and that style is theoretically well-suited to tracking Getaway Jewel, though the P8 in recent form is a concern and Callum Pritchard has limited big-race experience.

runners_data.name: Tropical Talent
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with 1 win and 6 places on good going from 13 similar runs — a respectable record — but his true instinct is to be held up and he will find himself racing in midfield ahead of his comfort zone; Jack Tudor is a high-class jockey who may manage the situation well, but the style mismatch is a genuine discount to his prospects.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Tropical Talent carries 149 lb into this, though he does arrive fresh on a nine-day turnaround, has experience over today's trip and going, and posted a second last time out.

runners_data.name: Peace Motivator
runners_data.note: A six-year-old with a deeply concerning recent record of multiple pulled-up efforts (P-PP8P), and trainer Barry John Murphy has no winners from 7 runners in the past fortnight; despite handling good ground in previous runs, the pattern of non-completions is alarming and his redistribution into midfield from a natural rear position adds further tactical difficulty — the evidence does not support optimism.
runners_data.comment: Peace Motivator has run over today's trip and going, our rating of 99 marks him out as a significant threat despite carrying 143 lb, but his recent record — four pull-ups in his last five starts — is a serious concern that connections must overcome.

races.paceDynamic: Getaway Jewel is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with Brian Hughes in the saddle, will stride into a clear lead from the off and control fractions at a sustainable, uncontested clip over the 2m½f trip on good ground at Sedgefield. With no genuine pressing rival to push Getaway Jewel off her rhythm, the pace is likely to be measured rather than gruelling, meaning the race will be run to suit those tracking close behind rather than those forced to make up ground from deep. The field is heavily stacked with hold-up types — Dexter, American Empire, Tropical Talent and Peace Motivator are all natural hold-up horses who have been redistributed to midfield because there is simply no room for all of them to settle as far back as they would prefer, meaning the rear of the field will be congested and their late runs may be compromised. A controlled tempo with a lone pace-setter strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader without burning energy early, then challenge from a position of superiority in the home straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Getaway Jewel Controls and Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Getaway Jewel is allowed to dictate an unchallenged, measured gallop and none of the prominent horses have the class to reel her in late.
scenarios.body: Getaway Jewel has won and placed repeatedly on good ground at this sort of distance and, with a 12-year-old's tactical savvy under Hughes, she will know exactly how to husband her stamina over the final fences; horses who race prominently and close in second or third will be best placed to challenge, but catching a fresh-legged leader at this class level is tough.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent chasers sits close to the controlled pace throughout and picks off a tiring Getaway Jewel after the final fence.
scenarios.body: Applejack Poet, who has consistent form on good going over this sort of trip, is ideally suited to track and pounce, and Hooper — despite hold-up tendencies — has placed six times and handles good ground well enough to make a sustained late challenge from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Getaway Jewel sets an unexpectedly quick early pace that strings the field out and softens the front-runners, allowing a hold-up horse to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: Dexter and American Empire are the most likely beneficiaries in this shape, both having genuine late-running form on good ground, but the redistribution of so many hold-up types into midfield means they will be jostling with rivals for position rather than travelling smoothly, reducing the probability of a clean run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Outsider Profits
scenarios.trigger: If there is a flurry of jumping errors or fallers that disrupts the pace and creates a messy, unpredictable finish.
scenarios.body: Socks Off, who has shown consistent placed form over various trips on good ground and is fresh from a 232-day break which may have freshened her, could profit from a chaotic scenario, while Peace Motivator has form on good going but has produced too many pulled-up efforts recently to be trusted.

watchPoints.text: Getaway Jewel — if Brian Hughes allows her to coast at a very slow pace through the first mile, the race will bunch and set up a sprint finish that could overwhelm her at the age of 12; watch whether any prominent runner pushes forward to test her in the early stages.

Congestion at the rear of the field — Dexter, American Empire, Tropical Talent and Peace Motivator are all hold-up types forced into midfield, meaning the group from fourth to eighth place will be tightly packed approaching fences, raising the risk of interference or jumping errors among rivals.

Socks Off — returning from 232 days off, she is an unknown quantity fitness-wise; if she shows any signs of blowing up or jumping slowly in the early stages, she becomes a danger to horses racing close to her in the midfield group.

Hooper's amateur jockey (7lb claimer Miss Amber Jackson-Fennell) is worth monitoring — in a tactical race where positioning off a slow pace is critical, the experience gap between her and Hughes (Getaway Jewel) could matter significantly in the home straight.

races.name: Sedgefield Racecourse For Outdoor Events Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Loriko
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR 125, Dan Skelton in excellent 9/23 T14 form with Harry Skelton aboard; front-running five-year-old with 8/10 similar-going record including two wins at this trip on Good, making him the dominant pace influence and the one to beat if he handles the early battle.
runners_data.comment: Loriko has won three of his last five starts, with victories last time out and two runs back from that — and a trainer firing at 39% in the past fortnight adds plenty of confidence. He has run over today's trip and going, and at 168 lb there is a weight question, but his recent form makes him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Skyjack Hijack
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old front-runner who wears a tongue-strap and has been off 61 days; Jennie Candlish's 1/15 T14 form is modest, and his recent record shows a string of P and fifth-place finishes — will be hard to suppress at the front but may lack the resolution to see it out under pressure at this OR.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and including two pulled-up efforts, Skyjack Hijack arrives here 61 days fresh, has run over today's trip and going, and carries 164 lb — the main risk is whether connections have found an explanation for those two non-completions.

runners_data.name: Ladies Day
runners_data.note: Five-year-old front-runner with progressive form (wins at 16f and 20f on Good) for trainer T Ellis, who has a tight 1/5 T14 book; 53 days since last run is manageable, and her 2/20f/GOO prior run confirms she stays this trip — a genuine lead threat who could pinch this if Loriko's connections ride a waiting race.
runners_data.comment: Ladies Day has won two of her last five starts, scoring back-to-back victories before a fourth last time out, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions; the 53-day absence is the one factor to weigh against her claims here.

runners_data.name: Glory And Honour
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up horse in first-time tongue-strap, backed by a 3/21 T14 trainer strike for Sam England and back quickly on just 12 days' rest; claiming jockey Miss Rebecca Hitchen takes 10lbs off the weights, and his most recent run was a win over this course and distance on Good — the chief beneficiary if the front three exhaust each other.
runners_data.comment: Glory And Honour ran a fine race last time, finishing second twelve days ago, and he has experience of both today's trip and going; the concern is that 154 lb is a hefty weight to carry.

runners_data.name: Ballygeary
runners_data.note: Veteran nine-year-old hold-up type running in a tongue-strap, off 53 days for Mike Sowersby whose T14 read is 0/5 — no wins in his last five runs (best a third), and his OR of 105 leaves him significantly outclassed at the top of the weights; likely needs everything to go perfectly to threaten.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Ballygeary is hard to fancy here, though a third one start back offers a sliver of encouragement; he has run over today's trip and going, and 53 days between runs leaves fitness an open question.

races.paceDynamic: Three confirmed front-runners — Loriko, Skyjack Hijack, and Ladies Day — will contest the lead from the outset over 2m4f at Sedgefield on Good ground, making a strong early gallop virtually inevitable. Loriko (Harry Skelton, Dan Skelton in strong 9/23 T14 form) is the classiest of the trio at OR 125 and will likely assert dominance up front, but Ladies Day and Skyjack Hijack will not surrender ground easily, ensuring genuine competition for the lead through the early stages. This contested pace over a stamina-testing trip on an undulating track will stretch the field significantly, burning off horses who cannot sustain jumping effort under pressure, and setting up a premium on resolution and staying power in the final half-mile. The race shape strongly favours a hold-up or patient tracking profile — Glory And Honour and Ballygeary both sit off the pace by nature, but with only five runners, the true beneficiary will be whichever of the front-running trio can handle the early battle and still quicken, or the hold-up horse with enough class to reel in a weakened leader late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Burns Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If Loriko overcomes the pace battle with Skyjack Hijack and Ladies Day and sustains his superiority to the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: The three-way tussle for the front sets a demanding gallop that tests all participants, but Loriko's superior OR (125) and Skelton's tactical intelligence allow him to dominate once rivals crack under the pressure of the trip. This scenario favours the highest-rated front-runner who can take the heat and find more when it matters, with the hold-up pair arriving too late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way pace battle truly burns out the front-runners and Glory And Honour or Ballygeary arrive powerfully from off the pace.
scenarios.body: The contested early gallop depletes Loriko, Skyjack Hijack, and Ladies Day in the closing stages, leaving the hold-up pair with a significant energy advantage approaching the last two hurdles. Glory And Honour's recent win (1/16f/GOO) and trainer Sam England's 3/21 T14 strike rate give this scenario genuine credibility if the pace is as fierce as expected.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If one of Ladies Day or Skyjack Hijack manages to slip the field or dictate at a more controlled tempo after rivals do not push as hard as expected.
scenarios.body: Should Loriko miss the break or Skelton elect to sit and the early pace become less contested, Ladies Day or Skyjack Hijack could exploit to control proceedings at a manageable tempo and find enough to hold on. Ladies Day's winning form at the trip (2/20f/GOO) and Skyjack Hijack's course experience make both capable of this if given a soft lead.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace Closers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is surprisingly moderate and the race turns into a sprint finish that rewards tactical sharpness over stamina.
scenarios.body: A falsely run affair at a small five-runner field would compress the field and set up a late dash, removing the stamina premium and potentially flattening the market. This is unlikely given three genuine front-runners present, but Glory And Honour's 10 claim-assisted campaign record shows the horse can quicken if conditions suit.

watchPoints.text: Loriko and Ladies Day — watch for an immediate battle for the rail and the front from the off; if they race head-to-head from the first, the pace could become truly punishing and significantly enhance Glory And Honour's chance of a late run.

Skyjack Hijack — off 61 days and wearing a tongue-strap, watch his jumping in the early stages; any errors or loss of rhythm at the first few flights under pressure from rival front-runners could see him drop away quickly and render him a non-factor.

Glory And Honour — returning on just 12 days' rest; if the quick turnaround leaves him below peak, the hold-up plan fails at its execution point, removing the main credible threat to the front-running trio in the closing stages.

Ballygeary — trainer Mike Sowersby has zero winners from five T14 runners; monitor market moves for any sign of stable confidence, as his hold-up profile is only viable if the three front-runners produce an exceptionally strong pace and he finds more than his recent form suggests.

races.name: Fairlight Studios Cafe @ Sedgefield Racecourse Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Dr Seb
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Mike Sowersby, 47 days since last run and fresh, with two wins on good ground in his last five similar-going runs; has form over 24f but stepping up to 3m3f tests whether he truly gets this trip, and Brian Hughes will need to judge the fractions expertly over the extra distance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and pulled up most recently, Dr Seb returns after 47 days but has experience of today's going and a rating of 109 puts him clear of his rivals at the top of the rankings, making him the one to side with despite that concerning latest run.

runners_data.name: East Eagle
runners_data.note: Strong course specialist with two wins at Sedgefield over 26f on good going and an 11/15 record on similar ground; Charlie Maggs (3lb claim) is a tactical advantage, and this 6-year-old's hold-up style is perfectly suited to hunting down a lone front-runner over this staying trip — his natural closing style is entirely authentic here.
runners_data.comment: East Eagle won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a genuine threat under 162 lb; the main concern is that pulled-up run two starts back leaves a fitness question after 52 days off.

runners_data.name: Lipstick Traces
runners_data.note: Recent run 12 days ago (LR:12d) keeps her fit but her form string of -35F57 includes a fall and several modest efforts; she is a hold-up type on good ground but her stepping up to 3m3f from shorter trips in her history raises a stamina question, and Callum Bewley will need to produce a career-best effort.
runners_data.comment: Ranked second of six in our assessment, Lipstick Traces has going experience to call on and returns in sharp order just 12 days since her last start, though the chief concern is a run of five starts without a win in recent form.

runners_data.name: Moro Rock
runners_data.note: Second prominent type in the field who gives Dr Seb some potential company early, though 82 days off the track is notable; Sara Ender's runner has a consistent record on good ground over marathon trips (1W6P in 15 similar-going runs), and his place prospects improve if the pace becomes a real stamina slog in the closing stages.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked fifth of six on our figures, Moro Rock heads here on a lengthy 82-day break carrying 149 lb, making him hard to fancy; a third two starts back is the sole encouragement, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Luminaries
runners_data.note: Disappointing recent form (99-077) and naturally a rear-of-field operator by preference; the field composition means he's mapped to midfield rather than his natural position at the back, so his true hold-up style is compromised here — headgear (tb) and a trainer running at 1/11 over 14 days adds further caution to a horse whose similar-going record (3W5P in 15) flatters what his current form suggests.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 45 days off, Luminaries carries 145 lb on going he has encountered before, and a rating of 85 suggests he holds claims — though his recent string of modest finishes is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Time Was
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby is in decent 14-day form (2/12) but Time Was brings a 0W1P record on similar going from 15 attempts and a form string of 4-P858 that signals no obvious winning chance; a genuine back-of-field type by preference, racing in a position that doesn't come naturally in this field, with headgear (tp) offering limited encouragement given recent efforts.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Time Was faces a stiff task here; she has experience of today's going and returns after 51 days off, but a pulled up and two eighths in recent starts make her hard to fancy at 142 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Dr Seb is the confirmed front-runner and, with only Moro Rock as a second prominent type, will dictate alone from the front over this 3m3f trip at Sedgefield on good ground — a sustainable, uncontested gallop is the most likely shape. With no horse willing or able to genuinely challenge Dr Seb for the lead, the pace will be controlled rather than pressured, suiting a horse that can travel smoothly and conserve energy for the final circuit. East Eagle, Lipstick Traces, Luminaries, and Time Was are all hold-up types by nature, meaning the field will be strung out behind a lone pace-setter with little tactical disruption until they hunt him down late. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with the stamina to close over 3m3f on good ground — specifically those with genuine staying credentials who can reel in a well-rested front-runner who has had it all his own way. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can place at the rear — Luminaries and Time Was are true closers redistributed to midfield on the map, but East Eagle, who has strong course form and is a genuine hold-up performer, is best placed to exploit the controlled tempo from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Solo Lead Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Dr Seb gets an uncontested lead and the hold-up horses fail to close the gap in time over the staying trip.
scenarios.body: Dr Seb sets a measured pace throughout, conserving energy and jumping economically, with no rival willing to pressurise him at any stage; on good ground over 3m3f, a fresh horse (47 days off) controlling his own fractions gives him a genuine chance of lasting to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Reels In
scenarios.trigger: If the closers, led by East Eagle, time their run perfectly and overhaul a tiring Dr Seb in the final two flights.
scenarios.body: East Eagle's excellent course form (two wins over similar distances at Sedgefield on good ground) puts him in an ideal position to track the controlled pace and deliver a well-timed challenge; his 11/15 record on similar going reinforces his credentials as the most likely beneficiary if Dr Seb's fractions prove just too slow to hold on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Grind Suits Stayer
scenarios.trigger: If the pace picks up significantly on the final circuit turning this into a genuine stamina test that exposes those out of their comfort zone.
scenarios.body: Moro Rock's record of hitting the frame over marathon trips on good ground makes him a live contender if endurance becomes the dominant factor; horses like Luminaries and Time Was, already out of their natural hold-up roles, will struggle to get competitive from off a pace they haven't been able to dictate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Outgunned Late
scenarios.trigger: If Luminaries or Time Was, racing out of their true hold-up role, make significant late headway to challenge.
scenarios.body: Both Luminaries and Time Was are genuine rear-of-field types pushed into midfield by the field's composition, meaning they are unlikely to reproduce their best form from a position that doesn't suit them; their recent form figures (9s, 7s, 8s) reinforce that they are unlikely to deliver the winning run even if the shape theoretically opens a late lane.

watchPoints.text: East Eagle is the main danger to Dr Seb's lead — watch whether Charlie Maggs positions him close enough to the pace on the final circuit to deliver a telling late challenge, as his two Sedgefield wins suggest he knows exactly how to run this track.

Dr Seb's stamina at 3m3f is unproven in his recent form history — if Brian Hughes goes too fast early trying to build an unassailable lead, he risks emptying in the final half-mile and being caught by the field.

Moro Rock's 82-day absence is the longest layoff in this field — watch his jumping and early movement for any signs of rustiness that might compromise his ability to track the front-runner effectively from a prominent pitch.

Luminaries and Time Was are both racing out of their preferred hold-up positions due to the field's composition — if neither settles naturally in the first mile, energy wastage early could render their finishing kicks academic by the time they reach the home straight.

The going is a consistent Good across all seven races at Sedgefield today — no race-to-race deterioration to factor in, meaning ground conditions will not provide any unexpected advantage or disadvantage for any runner in this field.

races.name: Whitegates Nursery Northallerton Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Pergamon
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's hold-up horse arrives in sharp form after four wins in his last five, all on good ground, but the sedate pace set by a lone front-runner in a four-runner field may leave him too much to do from the rear, even with William Shanahan claiming 5lb.
runners_data.comment: Pergamon arrives on the back of three consecutive wins and, despite a 53-day break, his recent dominance makes him the pick here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 162 lb is the main question against his excellent recent profile.

runners_data.name: King Ulanda
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor's mount has a strong claim as the closest pursuer with a 9/15 good-ground record and a recent win; his prominent style means he will shadow Max Of Stars naturally and his course profile gives genuine grounds for optimism if the leader weakens late.
runners_data.comment: King Ulanda arrives on the back of a win last time out and boasts another victory three starts back, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour; the main concern is the 56-day absence.

runners_data.name: Max Of Stars
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and race-shaper — Brian Hughes will set an uncontested tempo from the gate; recent form of 13U-44 is modest but his 13/15 good-ground record underlines suitability, and he ran just 18 days ago so is race-fit and ready to exploit a trouble-free lead.
runners_data.comment: Rated 117 and top of the rankings, Max Of Stars brings distance and going experience and returns fit after 18 days, but her most recent outings show back-to-back fourths, and the main risk is whether she can recapture the winning form she showed five starts back.

runners_data.name: Saint Polo
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago which is an aggressive turnaround and bears watching for any signs of fatigue; Luke Scott claims 3lb and the horse has three recent wins to his name, but his hold-up style and a potential energy deficit from such a quick reappearance make him the hardest to assess.
runners_data.comment: Saint Polo arrives in red-hot form — a winner on three of his last five starts, with back-to-back victories before finishing third last time out — and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the main concern is a gruelling 156 lb on his back off just two days' rest.

races.paceDynamic: Max Of Stars is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just four runners, will bowl along uncontested from the off on good ground at Sedgefield — Brian Hughes can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop without any rival capable of stretching him early. King Ulanda is the only prominent-style runner and will likely sit just off Max Of Stars in second, leaving Pergamon and Saint Polo to track from off the pace in a small, compact field. With no pace pressure, Max Of Stars can conserve energy through the early stages and present a moving target at the business end — the lack of genuine pace rivalry means the gallop is unlikely to be strong enough to string the field out. This race shape heavily favours the front-running and prominent profiles: hold-up horses Pergamon and Saint Polo will need Max Of Stars to empty quickly off a steady tempo, which is far from guaranteed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Max Of Stars bowls along at a sustainable clip and King Ulanda sits close without forcing the issue, the leader retains enough reserves to see out the 2m1f trip.
scenarios.body: Max Of Stars sets his own pace under Hughes, jumps accurately, and simply has too much left in the tank for rivals who are forced to make up ground from hold-up positions on a gallop that was never truly demanding; King Ulanda, the closest pursuer throughout, is best placed to pick up any late weakness.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively strong enough to drain Max Of Stars in the final half-mile, freeing the hold-up pair to charge home.
scenarios.body: Pergamon arrives with a strong late run having won four of his last five and clearly relishes good ground, while Saint Polo has also shown sharp finishing form with three recent wins; both need Max Of Stars to have done enough damage to himself in front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent King Ulanda Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If King Ulanda travels strongly in Max Of Stars' slipstream and produces a decisive jump at the last to collar the leader.
scenarios.body: Jack Tudor slots King Ulanda into an ideal stalking position and the horse's good-ground form (winning on all five good-ground starts in his history) gives him the platform to strike when asked; he has the form and fitness to exploit any late fade from the front-runner.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Favourite
scenarios.trigger: If a jumping error or incident disrupts Max Of Stars, forcing an unplanned reshuffle in this tiny field.
scenarios.body: With only four runners any mishap at a hurdle scrambles the race entirely and opens the door for any of the hold-up pair to take advantage, with Pergamon's consistent recent form giving him the edge in a scramble.

watchPoints.text: Max Of Stars — if he jumps cleanly and settles into a rhythm under Hughes, the uncontested lead in a race of only four runners makes him very difficult to pass, particularly if the tempo is never genuinely pressured.

Saint Polo — a two-day turnaround (LR:2d) is unusually quick and connections should be watched at the start; any visible signs of fatigue or reluctance could see him run well below his recent winning form.

Pergamon — despite brilliant recent form, the hold-up style is tactically disadvantaged here; watch whether Shanahan elects to push forward early to avoid being marooned in a small field on a non-searching gallop.
King Ulanda — his fall in recent form string (F6-141) is worth noting as a jumping risk at Sedgefield; if he makes a significant error, the race effectively becomes a solo affair for Max Of Stars.

Sedgefield good ground is confirmed across all seven cards today — no unexpected surface deterioration to factor in, meaning all four runners encounter conditions consistent with their good-ground form histories.
